summary: Eighting and Hudson Soft's 3D fighting series built around zoanthrope beast transformations.

emulation.notes: Use PS1 emulation or PSN-owned copy for the complete home feature set.

primary.why: The arcade original introduced the series as Beastorizer in North America, but the PlayStation version adds home modes, PlayStation-exclusive Beast Rave, and a later North American PSN route. It is the most complete practical version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on original hardware, PS3/PSP/Vita PSN where owned, or DuckStation with upscaling.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Sony ZN-1 arcade release, known as Beastorizer in North America.
all_releases.reason: skip: original cabinet baseline, but PlayStation adds exclusive modes and later PSN access.

all_releases.fidelity: Home release with extra modes and PlayStation-exclusive Beast Rave, later re-released on North American PSN.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is the original fidelity route; PlayStation is more complete for modes and accessibility.

emulation.notes: Use PS1 emulation or PSN-owned copy.

primary.why: Bloody Roar 2 shipped to arcades and then PlayStation, with the PlayStation version later available through the North American PlayStation Network for PS3, PSP, and Vita. It is the practical home route for the full sequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version on original hardware, PSN where owned, or DuckStation with upscaling.

all_releases.reason: skip: original cabinet route, but PlayStation is the complete home version.

all_releases.fidelity: Home release, later available through North American PSN on PS3/PSP/Vita.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is original; PlayStation/PSN is the practical home route.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for high-resolution PS2 play.

primary.why: Bloody Roar 3 was built on Namco System 246 arcade hardware and ported to PlayStation 2. With no later home revision documented for this specific entry, the PS2 version is the best complete home route and can be upscaled in PCSX2.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscale.

all_releases.reason: skip: original cabinet route, but PS2 is the practical home version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is original, while PS2 is the playable home route with emulator upscale potential.

entries.title: Bloody Roar Extreme / Primal Fury
entries.definitive_edition: Bloody Roar Extreme on Xbox plus GameCube presentation supplement

emulation.notes: Use xemu or original Xbox for the primary; use Dolphin or Wii backward compatibility for the GameCube supplement.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox or high-resolution GameCube/Xbox emulation

primary.why: Primal Fury/Extreme expands on Bloody Roar 3 with new arenas, remodeled levels, new character models, and move-set changes. The Xbox version keeps hidden character Fang available in North American and European releases, making it the most complete gameplay route, while the GameCube version preserves the original animated cutscenes.
primary.how_to_play: Play Bloody Roar Extreme on original Xbox or a compatible Xbox emulator; check the GameCube version separately if you want the original animated opening/ending presentation.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original animated opening and ending presentation
secondary.what_to_play: Watch or sample the GameCube Primal Fury presentation if you care about the original anime-style cutscenes.
secondary.why: The Xbox version replaces those cutscenes with pre-rendered CG sequences.

all_releases.fidelity: Bloody Roar: Primal Fury, the intended GameCube release with original animated opening/endings.
all_releases.reason: secondary: presentation supplement; Xbox has broader Fang availability.

all_releases.fidelity: Bloody Roar Extreme port with CG cutscenes and Fang retained in North American/European releases.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete gameplay route due hidden character availability.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Xbox is the gameplay-complete pick because of Fang availability; GameCube keeps the original animated cutscenes and was the initially targeted hardware.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists; Xbox version is not backward compatible with Xbox 360.

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for high-resolution PS2 play.

primary.why: Bloody Roar 4 was released only on PlayStation 2, with the largest roster in the series and a beast gauge that acts as a separate health meter. No alternate edition is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 version on original hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscale.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one documented platform route exists.
